correctness.rationale: The exact mass-normalized active-set decomposition and Cauchy bound reduce the nonlinear norm to the Perron eigenvalue of an explicit 2x2 matrix (trace 2-t, determinant (1-t)^2). An admissible two-level positive Perron vector saturates it for each subset, proving optimality and the full extremizer characterization. Strict unimodality yields one-third equality. A polynomial-size positive-integer subset-sum reduction and NP membership establish weak NP-completeness. Computations from the actual Python file independently corroborate 153 exact algebraic identities, 210 extremizers, and 320 small reductions.

originality.rationale: The novelty is limited to arbitrary unequal positive atomic masses, optimal attainable-mass subsets, and the arithmetic/weak NP-complete equality criterion. Theorem 4 of arxiv:2005.03146 fully covers the equal-weight subfamily and is explicitly treated as prior art, not as new. The extant uniform-counting formula does not imply the constrained weighted mass-spectrum formula: cloning unequal weights allows forbidden splitting of atomic clones. Relevant accessible original proofs and nearby literature were compared as statements. Unindexed weighted formulations remain a material residual risk.
residual_risks: A weighted finite-atomic maximal-operator theorem may exist under alternate notation or in unindexed literature; absence of matches is not proof of priority.

The weighted two-level Cauchy method is closely adapted from the known uniform-counting proof; novelty pertains to the arbitrary mass-subset dependence and NP-complete equality criterion, not to the unweighted sharp constant.
The sequel arxiv:2011.02630 was not read cover-to-cover; its accessible introduction specifies counting measure, but full-text noncoverage is not asserted.

An exact sharp finite-atom theorem for two-stage nonnegative martingale maxima, if located, could dominate the present weighted-complete-graph formulation; no covering such statement was found in searched material.

value.rationale: The precise natural invariant is the centered strong Hilbert maximal norm on an arbitrary positive atomic metric-measure complete graph. The theorem evaluates it fully by the reachable subset-mass spectrum, classifies every extremizer and describes exactly when a universal sharp bound is achieved. Attainment is genuinely arithmetic: [1,2] achieves the bound with two atoms, [1,1,2] does not with three, and the exact-equality decision for binary positive integer masses is weakly NP-complete. A pseudo-polynomial algorithm is available but no polynomial algorithm is implied; this differentiates the finding from routine equal-counting-mass substitution.
